# CAST — Groundwater Contamination Assessment {.unnumbered}

**CAST** (Contamination Assessment and Site management Tool) is a browser-based
research platform for assessing groundwater quality and setting up contaminant
transport models for BTEX-type contamination. It brings a site database,
analytical, empirical and numerical transport models, and an analytic-element
source designer together in one workflow — from field measurements to a
communicable result.

CAST is aimed at the **preliminary risk evaluation** of sites that have not yet
been assessed. It lets a user explore a site, run appropriate models, and reach
an early site-assessment decision without stitching together separate tools.

## The toolboxes

CAST is organised into toolboxes that are designed to be used in sequence:

| Toolbox | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Site Database** | Manage, visualize, and analyze site measurements. Includes 100+ reference sites and supports user uploads. |
| **Analytical Models** | Closed-form plume solutions — Liedl 2D & 3D, Chu, Ham, Cirpka, and BIOSCREEN-AT. |
| **Empirical Models** | Field-data correlations for plume length — Maier & Grathwohl, Birla et al. |
| **Numerical Models** | MODFLOW / MT3D-based flow & transport simulations, in horizontal and vertical setups. |
| **AEM Source Designer** | Analytic-element source geometry, forward simulation, and inverse parameter estimation. |

## Suggested workflow

1. Start with the **Site Database** toolbox to load and validate site data.
2. Continue with an **Analytical** or **Empirical** model for a fast first estimate.
3. Run the **Numerical** model toolbox for a spatially resolved simulation.
4. Use the **AEM Source Designer** for source-geometry and parameter estimation.

## How CAST is built

CAST is a [Flask](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/) web application. Interactive
model pages are served as [HoloViz Panel](https://panel.holoviz.org/) apps;
numerical simulations run on [MODFLOW 6](https://www.usgs.gov/software/modflow-6)
via [FloPy](https://flopy.readthedocs.io/); site data lives in MySQL. The whole
stack — nginx → Flask/Gunicorn + Panel → MySQL — ships as a Docker Compose
project, so a full instance runs with a single command (see
[Run CAST locally](contents/start/run_locally.qmd)).

::: {.callout-note}
CAST is a work in progress. Not every toolbox or model is fully implemented, and
some interactivity is still limited — but the current state is already a useful
assessment application.
:::
